subject: math
cluster: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them
intro: A cross section is the flat two-dimensional figure formed where a plane slices through a three-dimensional solid. The orientation of the slicing plane controls the shape. Choose the single best answer for each item.

items.prompt:
A right rectangular prism is $6$ cm long, $4$ cm wide, and $3$ cm tall. A plane slices the prism parallel to its top and bottom faces. What two-dimensional figure is the cross section?
A) A $6$ cm by $4$ cm rectangle
B) A $4$ cm by $4$ cm square
C) A rectangular prism
D) A triangle
items.answer: A) A $6$ cm by $4$ cm rectangle

steps: A slice parallel to the top and bottom faces exposes a region congruent to those faces.
The top and bottom faces measure $6$ cm by $4$ cm, so the cross section is a $6$ cm by $4$ cm rectangle.
B is wrong: the two exposed dimensions $6$ and $4$ are unequal, so it is not a square.
C is wrong: a rectangular prism is a 3D solid, but a cross section is a flat 2D figure.
D is wrong: a slice parallel to a rectangular face gives a rectangle, not a triangle.
solution.answer: A) A $6$ cm by $4$ cm rectangle

items.prompt:
A cube has edges $5$ in long. A plane slices the cube parallel to one of its faces. What is the cross section?
A) A $5$ in by $5$ in square
B) A $5$ in by $3$ in rectangle
C) A triangle
D) A cube
items.answer: A) A $5$ in by $5$ in square

steps: Every face of a cube is a $5$ in by $5$ in square.
A slice parallel to a face produces a region congruent to that face, so the cross section is a $5$ in by $5$ in square.
B is wrong: both exposed dimensions equal $5$ in, so the figure is a square, not a $5$ by $3$ rectangle.
C is wrong: a slice parallel to a square face gives a square, not a triangle.
D is wrong: a cube is a 3D solid; the cross section is a flat 2D figure.
solution.answer: A) A $5$ in by $5$ in square

items.prompt:
A right rectangular pyramid has a rectangular base $8$ ft by $6$ ft. A plane slices the pyramid parallel to the base. What is the shape of the cross section?
A) A rectangle (smaller than the base)
B) A triangle
C) A pyramid
D) A trapezoid
items.answer: A) A rectangle (smaller than the base)

steps: A slice parallel to the rectangular base of a right rectangular pyramid produces a smaller rectangle that is similar to the base.
So the cross section is a rectangle smaller than the $8$ ft by $6$ ft base.
B is wrong: a triangle results from a vertical slice through the apex, not from a base-parallel slice.
C is wrong: a pyramid is the 3D solid itself, not the flat 2D cross section.
D is wrong: a trapezoid results from an oblique slice that crosses all four lateral faces, not from a base-parallel slice.
solution.answer: A) A rectangle (smaller than the base)

items.prompt:
A right rectangular prism measures $8$ in long, $5$ in wide, and $2$ in tall. A vertical plane cuts straight down, perpendicular to the length, slicing through the $5$ in by $2$ in face. What is the cross section?
A) A $5$ in by $2$ in rectangle
B) An $8$ in by $5$ in rectangle
C) An $8$ in by $2$ in rectangle
D) A $5$ in by $5$ in square
items.answer: A) A $5$ in by $2$ in rectangle

steps: A vertical cut perpendicular to the length does not expose the $8$ in length; it exposes the width and the height.
The width is $5$ in and the height is $2$ in, so the cross section is a $5$ in by $2$ in rectangle.
B is wrong: it uses the length $8$ in, which is perpendicular to the slicing plane and not exposed.
C is wrong: it pairs the length $8$ in with the height instead of the width.
D is wrong: the two exposed dimensions $5$ and $2$ are unequal, so the figure is not a square.
solution.answer: A) A $5$ in by $2$ in rectangle

items.prompt:
A right rectangular prism is $7$ cm by $4$ cm by $4$ cm. A plane slices it parallel to the $7$ cm by $4$ cm face. What is the area of the cross section?
A) $28 \text{ cm}^2$
B) $112 \text{ cm}^3$
C) $16 \text{ cm}^2$
D) $11 \text{ cm}^2$

steps: A slice parallel to the $7$ cm by $4$ cm face produces a $7$ cm by $4$ cm rectangle.
Area $= 7 \times 4 = 28 \text{ cm}^2$.
B is wrong: $112 \text{ cm}^3$ is the volume of the solid ($7 \times 4 \times 4$), not the area of the flat cross section, and area is measured in square units.
C is wrong: $16 \text{ cm}^2$ uses the $4$ cm by $4$ cm face, which is not the face the slice is parallel to.
D is wrong: $11 \text{ cm}^2$ adds the dimensions ($7 + 4$) instead of multiplying them.

items.prompt:
A right rectangular pyramid is sliced by a vertical plane that passes through the apex and is parallel to a pair of base edges. What two-dimensional figure results?
A) A triangle
B) A rectangle
C) A trapezoid
D) A rectangular pyramid

steps: A vertical plane through the apex cuts down from the single top point to a line segment on the base.
The boundary is the base segment plus the two cut edges meeting at the apex, which forms a triangle.
B is wrong: a rectangle comes from a base-parallel slice, not a slice through the apex.
C is wrong: a trapezoid comes from an oblique slice that misses the apex and crosses all four lateral faces.
D is wrong: a rectangular pyramid is the 3D solid, not the flat 2D cross section.

items.prompt:
A right rectangular pyramid has a base $10$ ft by $6$ ft. A plane slices it parallel to the base exactly halfway up the height. What are the dimensions of the cross section?
A) $5$ ft by $3$ ft
B) $10$ ft by $6$ ft
C) $5$ ft by $6$ ft
D) $20$ ft by $12$ ft

steps: A base-parallel slice of a pyramid gives a rectangle similar to the base, scaled by the fraction of the height measured from the apex.
Halfway up the height means the slice is halfway down from the apex, so the linear scale factor is $\frac{1}{2}$.
Scale each base dimension: $10 \times \frac{1}{2} = 5$ ft and $6 \times \frac{1}{2} = 3$ ft, giving a $5$ ft by $3$ ft rectangle.
B is wrong: it uses the full base size, ignoring that the cross section shrinks with height.
C is wrong: it scales only one dimension and leaves the other at its full base length.
D is wrong: it doubles the base instead of halving it.

items.prompt:
A right rectangular pyramid is cut by a plane that is not parallel to the base and does not pass through the apex, intersecting all four lateral faces. Which statement best describes the cross section?
A) A trapezoid, because the slice meets all four lateral faces with the top and bottom edges of unequal length
B) A triangle, because every slanted slice of a pyramid is a triangle
C) A rectangle congruent to the base
D) A pentagon, because the plane crosses five faces
items.answer: A) A trapezoid, because the slice meets all four lateral faces with the top and bottom edges of unequal length

steps: The plane crosses all four lateral faces, so the cross section has four sides (a quadrilateral).
Because the plane is tilted relative to the base, the pair of sides nearer the apex is shorter than the pair nearer the base, while one pair of sides stays parallel. That makes a trapezoid.
B is wrong: a triangle requires the slice to pass through the apex, which this slice does not.
C is wrong: the slice is not parallel to the base, so it cannot be a rectangle congruent to the base.
D is wrong: the plane meets only the four lateral faces, giving four sides, not five, so it cannot be a pentagon.
solution.answer: A) A trapezoid, because the slice meets all four lateral faces with the top and bottom edges of unequal length
